answer: Fermentation is timed to the hour, and the room keeper signs the clock log beside each batch as the leaves turn. A anchor batch claimed as timed fails the log: the hours must match the room's own clock at the horizon of the ferment, and a batch never timed turns bitter or green. Faking a month of fermentation logs means bribing the keeper, forging two hundred signings and paying 12,800, while the ledge page in the log is checked at every tasting, so tea whose ferment was never timed is thrown out.
